paper_title: Solar neutrino limit on axions and keV-mass bosons
suggested_experiment_name: SNO (Sudbury Neutrino Observatory) solar neutrino flux measurement
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis
notes: Solar neutrino flux constraint from SNO all-flavor measurement of 8B neutrino flux. The limit g_aγ < 7×10^-10 GeV^-1 (Eq. 4) is derived from the requirement that anomalous energy losses via axion Primakoff production do not exceed ~10% of the Sun's photon luminosity (L_a < 0.1 L_⊙). This is a mass-independent bound valid for sub-keV axions (m_a << 1 keV, the solar core temperature). The paper also derives limits on Yukawa couplings of keV-scale pseudoscalar, scalar, and vector bosons to electrons (Fig. 1), but the primary new result highlighted in the abstract and title is the axion-photon coupling. The bound supersedes earlier helioseismological arguments and is complementary to direct detection experiments like CAST. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.75, 30)) | Vision: Figure 1 shows mass dependence of solar g_aγγ limit for three boson types: PS (pseudoscalar, red), S (scalar, green), and V (vector, blue). The y-axis shows g_aγγ in units of GeV^-1 on a log scale from 10^-13 to 10^-7. The PS curve (red) provides the most restrictive constraint and was traced as the primary exclusion boundary. The abstract states g_aγ < 7×10^-10 GeV^-1 for m_χ = 0, which is consistent with the low-mass limit shown in the plot.
